scope: Sargent and Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2 (General States), Chapter 7: Recursive Decision Processes. RDPs (Gamma, V, B) with monotonicity (7.2) and consistency (7.3), the generated ADP, greedy policies (7.10) and the Bellman operator (7.11); examples (finite MDPs, firm valuation with bounded and unbounded profits, savings, Kreps-Porteus savings, modified rewards, risk-sensitive MDPs; Exercises 7.1.1-7.1.4), LDPs as RDPs (7.9) and isomorphic RDPs (Exercise 7.1.5); greedy policies for finite and continuous actions (Lemmas 7.1.1-7.1.2); bounded contractions (Propositions 7.2.1-7.2.2) and weighted contractions on b_l X (Lemma 7.2.3, Propositions 7.2.4-7.2.5, Theorem A.5.24 by transport); monotone and concave value functions and unique continuous optimal policies (Exercise 7.2.1, Propositions 7.2.6-7.2.8, Lemma A.2.6); risk measures and certainty equivalents (Exercises 7.2.5-7.2.6, Example 7.2.1, coherence of the mean and the pessimistic certainty equivalent, the entropic certainty equivalent, Kreps-Porteus expectations fail cash invariance); MDPs with continuous certainty equivalents (Proposition 7.2.10); optimal savings with utility unbounded above (Exercises 7.3.1-7.3.2, 7.2.2-7.2.4); irreversible investment under risk neutrality, risk aversion and ambiguity (Propositions 7.3.1-7.3.2, Exercise 7.3.3, Example 7.3.1, Section 7.3.3.2); multiplicative Kreps-Porteus and risk-sensitive RDPs are isomorphic (Exercise 7.3.4); with the earlier chapters' ADP, Banach lattice and LDP theory restated.
source: Thomas J. Sargent and John Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2: General States, Chapter 7, pp. 207-245, with the Appendix A results used there.
